name: Tiefo-D
catalog_citation: Heath, Jeffrey & Aminata Ouattara. 2021. A Grammar of Tiefo-D of Daramandugu (Niger-Congo language, Burkina Faso). Language Description Heritage Library; Zenodo record 4715103 (BW PDF).
catalog_locator: sec. 3.6 Tones, p.79; sec. 3.5 Cliticization, p.75; sketch sec. 2.1.2 Tones and prosody, p.7
catalog_quote: 3.6 Tones: There are three tone levels, H[igh], M[id], and L[ow]. None of these can be reduced to an allophone of one of the others. There is no evidence in favor of an accentual interpretation of tones. Contour tones on individual syllables, other than those due to vv-Contraction across boundaries. are <HL> and <LH>. ... 3.5 Cliticization: Tiefo-D belongs to the set of languages that have a) fixed word order, b) numerous grammatical particles, and c) no stress or accent shifts due to addition of a morpheme. In such languages, it can be difficult to distinguish cliticization from simple linear juxtaposition. ... 2.1.2 Tones and prosody: Tiefo-D has three tone levels, high, mid, and low, like several other languages of SW Burkina.

audit.reasoning: The record codes Tiefo-D as 'tonal' (no word stress) on the basis of Heath & Ouattara 2021, a 759-page open-access reference grammar that is the newest and most thorough description of the language and the top item in Glottolog's descriptive bibliography. I opened the held text file and confirmed all three deciding quotations verbatim at the cited printed pages (p.79 sec. 3.6, p.75 sec. 3.5, p.7 sec. 2.1.2), and confirmed the negative claim that the phonology chapter contains no stress section (TOC: 3.6 Tones, 3.7 Intonation; 'Metrically based vocalic processes' 3.4.1 is Heath's template heading covering apocope/epenthesis/schwa lenition and says nothing about prominence). Zenodo confirms no newer version of the grammar exists.
